finding.claim: Git.ls_remote() checks unsafe options but never calls Git.check_unsafe_protocols() on its URL or positional arguments. A caller who passes an untrusted URL such as `ext::sh -c <cmd>` gets arbitrary command execution through git's ext:: remote helper. Clone, fetch, pull, push, archive, Remote.create and Remote.set_url all block this by default, so ls_remote is the one network-facing sibling without the check.
finding.source: Untrusted URL or remote string passed by an application as a positional argument to Git.ls_remote(*args), for example `repo.git.ls_remote(user_url)`.
finding.sink: self._call_process("ls_remote", *args, **kwargs) at git/cmd.py:1144, which runs `git ls-remote ext::sh -c ...`. The ext:: remote helper executes the embedded command.

trace.note: ls_remote(*args, allow_unsafe_options=False, **kwargs) is the entry; args are the attacker-influenced URL
Only check_unsafe_options runs, against unsafe_git_ls_remote_options (--upload-pack, --exec). The URL is not examined.
args are passed straight to _call_process, which executes git
check_unsafe_protocols exists and would reject `<transport>::<addr>`, but ls_remote never calls it
Sibling Remote.fetch calls check_unsafe_protocols; Remote.pull and Remote.push do the same, and the Repo.clone path calls it at git/repo/base.py:1531

finding.guards_checked: The option allowlist check at cmd.py:1141-1143 covers only --upload-pack and --exec, not URL schemes. No `--` separator or protocol.allow restriction is applied in ls_remote. There is no allow_unsafe_protocols parameter at all, so callers cannot opt in or out. The sibling checks in remote.py:1068-1071, 1126-1128 and 1202-1204, and repo/base.py:1531-1532, were read and are enforced. A caller that only passes trusted URLs is not affected. Findings are limited to code I read; I did not run it.
